verdict.rationale: Angular's CLI documents an official `ng e2e` command that builds and serves the app and then runs end-to-end tests, so e2e runs are tied to the framework's dev server. The evidence does not name a bundled first-party e2e test runner or show it works without extra setup; the only tool mention (Protractor) is a dated AngularJS-era community comment. Missing for 10: identification of an official or default e2e framework, evidence it works out of the box without adding a third-party runner, in-depth e2e setup docs, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can integrate official end-to-end testing tools that work out of the box with the framework's dev server

citations.quote: Builds and serves an Angular application, then runs end-to-end tests.
easy testing with Karma, Protractor and DI
